text: Outside the night was cold and wet. <break time="0.8s" /> But in the small parlor. <break time="0.8s" /> Of Laburnum Villa. <break time="0.8s" /> The fire burned brightly. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister White and his son Herbert. <break time="0.8s" /> Were playing chess. <break time="0.8s" /> While Missus White sat knitting quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> By the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing the gate bang loudly. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister White hurried to the door. <break time="0.8s" /> To welcome their guest. <break time="0.8s" /> The guest was Sergeant Major Morris. <break time="0.8s" /> A tall, strong soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had spent twenty one years in India. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> He told them stories. <break time="0.8s" /> Of wild scenes, brave deeds. <break time="0.8s" /> Wars, and strange peoples. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Mister White asked. <break time="0.8s" /> About a monkeys paw. <break time="0.8s" /> That Morris had once mentioned. <break time="0.8s" /> And the soldiers face became serious. <break time="0.8s" /> He took a small, dried paw. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of his pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that an old holy man. <break time="0.8s" /> Had put a spell on it. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to show that fate ruled peoples lives. <break time="0.8s" /> And that those who interfered with it. <break time="0.8s" /> Did so to their sorrow. <break time="0.8s" /> Morris said. <break time="0.8s" /> Three different men. <break time="0.8s" /> Could each have three wishes from it. <break time="0.8s" /> And Morris himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Had already had his three. <break time="0.8s" /> The first man had his three wishes. <break time="0.8s" /> He said quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> But his third wish was for death.
